On 2026-10-23, consumer `shubhodeep1/tele-funtoken-msg-scoring` final PR #3933 (`orchestrator/project-3928` → `main`) never recovered from a 24-file conflict. Three things went wrong:
- `.ai/validate.yml` was host-only, so every resolver run failed before a model ran.
- The integration judge posted three contradictory diagnoses.
- The poller kept dispatching on a head the review gate had capped, and escalation never fired because `gh pr edit` failed without `read:org`.

This PR implements changes 1–3 of the follow-up. Items 4–5 are only written up, as a plan doc for approval.

### 1. `.ai/validate.yml` take-base on integration-sync heads (`scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh`)
- On `orchestrator/project-*` heads, the prepare step takes the default branch's version of the allowlisted `.ai/` files. The allowlist is just `.ai/validate.yml`.
  - Stages `1 2 3`, `2 3` and `1 3` check out `MERGE_HEAD`'s regular blob.
  - Stage `1 2` honours the default branch's deletion.
  - Symlinks, non-regular blobs and other stage shapes stay fail-closed.
- `.ai/validate.yml` is committed consumer config, not a generated file. In the incident both sides edited it by hand (#4734 on the project branch, #4045 on `main`). Because taking `main`'s copy drops the project's edits, the dropped diff is posted on the PR once the merge commit exists, under a new `ai:ai-asset-take-base:v1` marker.
- When the take-base clears the last conflict, the commit waits for the integration fingerprint check, like the manifest and guard-hook cases. A guard-hook resolution that happens alongside a take-base waits too.
